title: Isolation Rules
subtitle: Inventory the sandbox / CC workspace isolation rules on the host's iptables chains and safely clean up the ones nobody owns any more.
scopeLine: Current deployment scope: {{scope}} ({{source}}). Only markers outside this scope that pass every check can be cleaned up.
empty: No isolation rule markers from this project were found on the chains.

orphan.title: Cleanable ({{count}})
orphan.hint: Every check passed: not this deployment's, no containers on the old bridge, no container claims the scope, and nothing is listening on the allowed endpoints.

blocked.title: Blocked ({{count}})
blocked.hint: There is evidence it is still in use, or this process cannot tell. When in doubt it stays — deleting too little is always the safer error.

self.title: In use by this deployment ({{count}})
self.hint: Markers this deployment is currently using. They never appear in the cleanable list.

network.occupied: Old network {{network}} (bridge {{bridge}}) still has {{count}} container(s): {{containers}}. CC workspace containers are long-lived and never switch networks on restart; removing this rule set's catch-all DROP lets them reach the host's internal network with no error and no log entry.

confirmDialog.title: Clean up orphaned isolation rules
confirmDialog.warning: About to delete all {{count}} rules carrying marker {{marker}} from the host's iptables chains. This cannot be undone.
confirmDialog.recheck: The backend re-evaluates the verdict before executing: if a container has re-joined the old bridge or the old deployment came back in the meantime, this request is rejected rather than carried out.
confirmDialog.label: Type the marker to confirm
confirmDialog.mismatch: Does not match the marker being cleaned up
